purpose: Hydroquinone is used to lighten dark spots, uneven skin tone, freckles, and patches caused by conditions like melasma, age spots, or sun damage. It is also used for skin darkening that can happen after acne or minor skin injuries. Think of it as a treatment that helps even out your skin color over time.
how_it_works: Your skin gets its color from a substance called melanin, which is made by special cells in your skin. Hydroquinone works by slowing down the process that makes melanin, so your skin gradually produces less of it in the treated areas. Over time, this causes those darker spots to fade and blend in better with the rest of your skin.
common_side_effects: Mild redness, dryness, or a slight burning or stinging feeling where you apply it. Some people notice mild itching or skin peeling at first. These effects are usually temporary and tend to get better as your skin adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Always use sunscreen during the day while using this product, because sun exposure can bring the dark spots right back. Do not use it on irritated, sunburned, or broken skin. Avoid getting it in your eyes, nose, or mouth. Long-term or overuse can sometimes cause a condition called ochronosis, which creates a bluish-gray darkening of the skin — this is why you should follow your doctor's instructions carefully and not use it longer than directed. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before using this product.
typical_dosing: Most people apply a thin layer to the affected dark spots once or twice a day, usually in the morning and at night. Gently rub it into just the dark area — you do not need to apply it all over your face. Results usually take 4 to 8 weeks to notice, so be patient and consistent. Your doctor will let you know how long you should use it.
